notes: USMLE Content Outline is the official 2026 outline and explicitly lists cat-scratch disease (Bartonella henselae) under primary infections of lymphoid tissue in the Blood & Lymphoreticular System.
USMLE Physician Tasks/Competencies directly supports a most-likely-diagnosis item under Diagnosis: Formulating the Diagnosis.

CDC About Cat Scratch Disease is dated March 23, 2026 and directly supports the cause, kitten/cat exposure, low-grade fever, inoculation papule/pustule, and tender regional lymph nodes 1–3 weeks after exposure.
CDC differential sources were checked at their current published versions for infectious mononucleosis, toxoplasmosis, tularemia, and sporotrichosis.

difficulty.rationale: The exposure-and-regional-node pattern is recognizable, but tularemia, toxoplasmosis, infectious mononucleosis, and lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis are clinically plausible alternatives that require discrimination by exposure route, lesion morphology, lymph-node distribution, and associated findings.

duplicate_gate.selector_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
duplicate_gate.selected_construct: Cat-scratch disease due to Bartonella henselae presenting as inoculation papule followed by regional lymphadenitis

option_audit.cat_scratch_disease: Uniquely integrates a child, recent kitten-claw skin inoculation, a local papule, low-grade fever, and ipsilateral tender axillary lymphadenopathy in the CDC-supported time window.
option_audit.infectious_mononucleosis: Can cause fever and lymphadenopathy, but the local inoculation papule and ipsilateral draining-node pattern are not the typical mono presentation; pharyngitis, cervical nodes, and hepatosplenomegaly are absent.
option_audit.toxoplasmosis: Cat exposure can mislead, but typical human acquisition involves food or accidental ingestion after cat-feces/soil exposure, and the local papule-to-draining-node sequence is not characteristic.
option_audit.ulceroglandular_tularemia: A credible inoculation-plus-node mimic, but the classic lesion is an ulcer and typical exposures are tick/deer-fly bites or handling infected animals; the well kitten, papule, low-grade fever, and classic CSD sequence make tularemia inferior.
option_audit.lymphocutaneous_sporotrichosis: A deliberately close inoculation mimic, including possible cat transmission, but typical cutaneous disease begins with a painless bump and progresses to additional lesions that may suppurate, ulcerate, and spread proximally; isolated tender regional lymphadenopathy with the CSD pattern is better explained by Bartonella.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A 12-year-old develops a papule where a kitten claw broke the skin, then low-grade fever and a tender ipsilateral axillary node about three weeks later. This reconstructs cat-scratch disease without relying on the option labels.
adversarial_second_pass.lexical_cue_attack: The first staged version explicitly used the word 'scratched' in the stem while the correct option was 'Cat-scratch disease'. This avoidable lexical cue was removed by rewriting the exposure as a kitten claw breaking the skin. A fresh post-edit duplicate gate was then run and remained clean.
adversarial_second_pass.tularemia_attack: Ulceroglandular tularemia can produce regional nodes after inoculation, but it usually has an inoculation-site ulcer and typical tick/deer-fly or infected-animal exposure. The presented kitten/papule/low-grade-fever sequence is more specific for CSD.
adversarial_second_pass.sporotrichosis_attack: Cat-associated sporotrichosis is a legitimate mimic, so it was not dismissed solely by cat exposure. The stronger discriminator is morphology and course: sporotrichosis typically creates a painless primary bump followed by additional proximal cutaneous lesions, whereas this vignette centers on a papule plus tender draining-node lymphadenitis.
adversarial_second_pass.toxoplasmosis_attack: The presence of a cat alone is insufficient for toxoplasmosis; CDC describes foodborne or accidental ingestion after cat-feces/soil exposure, not a local inoculation papule followed by a single draining nodal basin.
adversarial_second_pass.mononucleosis_attack: The age and fever could fit EBV, but the localized inoculation sequence and absence of pharyngitis, cervical adenopathy, and hepatosplenomegaly make EBV non-best.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The item does not assert diagnostic test thresholds, titers, treatment durations, antibiotic rules, or epidemiologic percentages. The three-week interval is within CDC's directly stated 1–3 week lymph-node window. The 3-cm node size is a vignette observation, not a diagnostic cutoff.
adversarial_second_pass.hidden_semantic_overlap_check: Three broad candidate rounds rejected multiple overlapping Blood/Diagnosis constructs. The selected cat-scratch construct then had zero expanded canonical hits, and both initial and post-cue-correction staged-item scans returned zero canonical hits against the 660 FINAL items. Q0661-Q0669 staged-approved constructs do not overlap this diagnosis.
